mainTopic: How to read time-words in a נדר: 'שנה' versus 'השנה', what a vow 'for a יובל' covers, and the start of the discussion of a vow 'until פסח'.
overview: The גמרא finishes trying to prove from the משנה about a leap year that 'a year' (שנה) means the same as 'this year' (השנה), and so 'a day' (יום) means the same as 'today' (היום). The proof is pushed away. The משנה really is about 'השנה', and its new point is that the leap month is included even though most years have none. Next comes a new question: if someone vows off wine 'for a יובל', is the fiftieth year included? To answer it, the גמרא brings a ברייתא where the רבנן say the יובל year is not counted in the next seven-year cycle, and רבי יהודה says it is. Each side attacks the other from a פסוק, 'six years you shall sow' against רבי יהודה and 'produce for three years' against the רבנן. רבי יהודה answers that both פסוקים speak about ordinary cycles. Finally, the גמרא turns to the משנה's vow 'until פסח' and starts asking what רבי מאיר holds. That question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Trying to prove that 'a year' means 'this year'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that the משנה about a leap year must be talking about someone who said 'שנה', so 'שנה' is like 'השנה', and the same should be true for 'יום' and 'היום'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the משנה means just what it says ('this year'), why would it need to tell us that? It is obvious. So it must mean he said 'a year'. That shows 'a year' is like 'this year', and so 'a day' should be like 'today'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof from the משנה about a vow for 'השנה' in a leap year. It says the משנה must really be talking about someone who said 'שנה', which would answer the earlier question about 'יום'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the person said 'השנה', it is obvious that the whole year, leap month included, is forbidden, so the משנה would be teaching nothing new. To give the משנה a real point, the גמרא reads it as a case of 'שנה'. If 'שנה' only lasts until the year ends, then 'יום' should only last until the day ends.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say. Opens a first possible reading that is about to be rejected.
Why do I need it said? Meaning: this is too obvious to teach.
Rather, is it not that... Brings the reading the גמרא wants to prove.
Apparently, so we see. Draws the conclusion of the proof.
Is like, is comparable to.

steps.confusionAlert: 'שנה' means 'a year' and 'השנה' means 'this year'. The whole argument depends on the little letter ה at the start, so watch for it.

phrases.english: If you say it is exactly as it teaches,
why do I need it to be said?
Rather, is it not a case where he said 'a year'?
Apparently, 'a year' is like 'this year',
and 'a day' also has the same law as 'today'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא כִּדְקָתָנֵי — לְמָה לִי לְמֵימְרָא? אֶלָּא לָאו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier attempt to settle the question about a vow for 'יום' by using the משנה about a leap year.
steps.raayaObject: That 'יום' means only until the end of the current day, just like 'היום'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: one who vows off wine 'השנה' and the year becomes a leap year is forbidden for the extra month too. The גמרא reads it as a case of 'שנה'.

steps.title: The proof is pushed away: the משנה really means 'this year'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה really is about 'השנה'. It still teaches something new: we do not assume a normal 12-month year.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the person really said 'this year'. You might have thought we follow most years, which have no leap month, so the vow lasts only 12 months. The משנה teaches us that it lasts until the year really ends, leap month included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from the previous step. It shows the משנה still has a point even if the person said 'השנה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 claimed 'השנה' would make the משנה obvious. The answer is that it is not obvious: since most years have no leap month, someone might think 'this year' means a standard 12 months. The משנה teaches that it means the real calendar year, so it tells us nothing about 'שנה' or 'יום'.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually. Brings back the original reading the גמרא had dropped.
You might have said. Introduces the wrong idea the source comes to correct.
Most years.
Adding a leap month to make a leap year.
It teaches us. Shows the new point the source is making.

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה about a leap year cannot prove anything about 'שנה' or 'יום'. It is really about 'השנה', and its new point is that the leap month is included.

phrases.english: No, really it is a case where he said 'this year',
and what might you have said?
Follow most years,
and they do not have a leap month in them,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 1 by giving the משנה a new point while keeping its plain wording.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof. The משנה is not about 'שנה', so it says nothing about 'יום'.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Step 1 assumed that a משנה about 'השנה' would be teaching something obvious. It is not obvious, because one might have followed most years, which are 12 months.

steps.title: New question: a vow off wine 'for a יובל'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if someone vows off wine 'for a יובל', is the fiftieth year itself included in the vow?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: if someone said 'Wine that I taste for a יובל is forbidden to me', what is the law? Does the fiftieth year count as part of the fifty years before it, or as coming after them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about time-words in vows, this time about a vow for 'a יובל'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יובל cycle is fifty years. The question is whether year fifty belongs inside the vow, together with the years before it, or stands outside it as the start of what comes after. If it is 'like before fifty', the vow covers fifty years. If it is 'like after fifty', it covers only forty-nine.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the חכמים. Opens a real unsolved question.
The Jubilee year, the fiftieth year of the cycle. Here it is used as a length of time in a vow.
What? Meaning: what is the law?
The fiftieth year.

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
If he said, 'Wine that I taste for a Jubilee' is forbidden to me, what is the law?
Is the fiftieth year like the years before fifty,
or like the years after fifty?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: אָמַר ״יַיִן שֶׁאֲנִי טוֹעֵם יוֹבֵל״ מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from vows of a 'day' or 'year' to a new time-word, a vow for 'a יובל'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the fiftieth year included in a vow 'for a יובל', or not?

steps.title: Bringing a ברייתא: the רבנן say יובל is not counted in the שמיטה cycle
steps.stepSummary: To answer the question, the גמרא brings a ברייתא with a dispute. The רבנן learn from the פסוק that the fiftieth year is counted only as year fifty, so it is not part of the seven-year cycle.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear a ברייתא where רבי יהודה and the רבנן argue. The פסוק says 'And you shall sanctify the fiftieth year.' You count it as year fifty, and you do not also count it as year one of the next cycle. So they said: the יובל year does not count toward the seven-year cycle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to help answer the יובל question. This step gives the view of the רבנן, and the גמרא is setting up a link between this dispute and the vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the רבנן, the fiftieth year is its own year. It is not also the first year of the next שמיטה cycle, so the next cycle starts in year fifty-one. This treats the fiftieth year as belonging to the old fifty-year unit, which is the issue in the vow question.

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute.
The חכמים, the majority view.
From here they said. A rule learned from the פסוק.
Counts toward the seven-year (שמיטה) cycle.

steps.confusionAlert: 'שבוע' here does not mean a week of days. It means a seven-year שמיטה cycle.

phrases.english: Come and hear,
as it is taught in a ברייתא, a dispute between רבי יהודה and the Rabbis:
'And you shall sanctify the fiftieth year.'
You count it as the fiftieth year,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה מוֹנֶה שְׁנַת חֲמִשִּׁים וְאַחַת.
phrases.english: but you do not count it as year fifty and also year one.
From here they said:
The Jubilee year does not count toward the seven-year cycle.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתַנְיָא פְּלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to help answer the question in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the fiftieth year belongs to the fifty years before it or to the years after it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on ויקרא 25:10. The רבנן hold that the יובל year is not counted in the next seven-year cycle.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the יובל year counts in the seven-year cycle
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees and says the יובל year is also counted as part of the next seven-year cycle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: the יובל year does count toward the seven-year cycle.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי יהודה's opposing view, which finishes laying out the dispute. The גמרא is setting up how this dispute connects to the vow question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the fiftieth year also serves as year one of the next שמיטה cycle. That treats the fiftieth year as the start of what comes after, the opposite of the רבנן in step 4. So the two sides line up with the two options in the vow question.
steps.whyThisMatters: The two views give two different answers to whether the fiftieth year belongs before or after, which is exactly what the vow question in step 3 asked.

phrases.english: רבי יהודה says:
The Jubilee year does count toward the seven-year cycle.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: יוֹבֵל עוֹלֶה לְמִנְיַן שָׁבוּעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the dispute that was opened in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יובל year counts as part of the following seven-year cycle.

steps.title: The Rabbis challenge רבי יהודה from 'six years you shall sow'
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן attack רבי יהודה: if the יובל year counts as year one of the next cycle, that cycle has only five planting years, but the תורה says six.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to רבי יהודה: The פסוק says 'Six years you shall sow your field', but by your counting there are only five!
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן challenge רבי יהודה's view using a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, the יובל year is also year one of the next seven-year cycle. But you may not plant during יובל, so that cycle would have only five planting years. This clashes with the פסוק that promises six years of sowing.

keyTerms.meaning: Six years you shall sow your field (ויקרא 25:3)
Doesn't it say...? (introduces a פסוק as a challenge)

phrases.english: They said to Rabbi Yehuda:
Doesn't the verse say
"Six years you shall sow your field"
But here there are only five!
phrases.notes: Right after יובל, year one is the יובל itself, when planting is forbidden, so only five planting years are left.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה: הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יהודה's view from Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's claim that the יובל year also counts as year one of the next cycle.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If so, the cycle after יובל would have only five sowing years, which contradicts the פסוק's 'six years'.

steps.title: רבי יהודה answers back with 'produce for three years'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה shows that the רבנן have the same kind of problem: before יובל, the crop would have to last four years, but the פסוק says three.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: By your own view, the פסוק says 'It shall bring forth produce for three years', but here there are four!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה does not answer yet. Instead he throws back a matching challenge against the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה promises that the year before שמיטה will produce enough food for three years. But by the רבנן's counting, before יובל you cannot plant in year 49 (שמיטה) or in year 50 (יובל). So the crop of year 48 would have to stretch over four years, not three.

keyTerms.meaning: According to your words (your own view has a problem too)
It shall bring forth produce for three years (ויקרא 25:21)
Produce, crops

phrases.english: He said to them: According to your words,
doesn't the verse say
"And it shall bring forth produce for the three years"
Here there are four!
phrases.notes: Before יובל, the crop of year 48 must last through year 49, year 50, and into year 51 until new crops grow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A counter-challenge: it answers Step 6 by showing the רבנן face the same problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's view that the יובל year is counted only as year fifty.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If so, the years before יובל need food for four years, but the פסוק promises produce for only three.

steps.title: Both verses refer to ordinary seven-year cycles
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the רבנן must explain their פסוק as talking about regular cycles, and he can explain his פסוק the same way. So neither פסוק decides the argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, you will have to say your פסוק is about the other seven-year cycles. For my view too, the פסוק can be about the other seven-year cycles.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives the answer that works for both sides: each פסוק talks about normal cycles, not the special cycle next to יובל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן must explain 'three years' as talking about regular שמיטה cycles, not the one right before יובל. By the same logic, 'six years you shall sow' talks about regular cycles, not the one right after יובל. So the פסוק cannot be used against רבי יהודה, and the argument stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (you must say instead...)
To set it up, to explain the פסוק as talking about a certain case
The years of the seven-year cycle
Mine too (my view can use the same answer)

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן and רבי יהודה disagree about whether the יובל year ends the old cycle or also starts the new one. This is the background the גמרא uses for the question from Step 3: is the fiftieth year included in a vow 'for a יובל'? If יובל ends the old cycle (רבנן), it is included. If it starts the new cycle (רבי יהודה), it is not.

phrases.english: Rather,
it can be explained as referring to the other seven-year cycles;
for mine too,
it can be explained as referring to the other seven-year cycles.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִיכָּא לְאוֹקֹמַהּ בִּשְׁאָר שְׁנֵי שָׁבוּעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 6 by using the answer the רבנן themselves need for Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the פסוק to ordinary cases (a parallel answer that works for both sides)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Six years you shall sow' applies to every cycle, including the one right after יובל, which would disprove רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק applies only to ordinary seven-year cycles, so it does not disprove רבי יהודה.

steps.title: A vow until פסח: what does רבי מאיר hold?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a vow 'until פסח' and begins asking whether רבי מאיר holds that a person does not include a certain time in his words.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Until פסח, he is forbidden...' Is this to say that רבי מאיר holds that a person does not put himself...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה and starts to work out what רבי מאיר's ruling tells us about how people mean their words. The sentence continues past this point, so this step is setting up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי מאיר rules about a vow until before פסח, and his ruling seems to show something about what a person has in mind when he names a deadline. The גמרא starts to draw that idea out ('למימרא...') about what a person 'puts himself' into. Questions that open with 'למימרא' often lead to testing the idea against another source.

keyTerms.meaning: Until פסח
Is this to say...? (drawing a conclusion from a ruling)
He holds (this is his view)
A person does not put himself into... (the rest of the phrase comes on the next amud)

phrases.english: "Until Pesach": he is forbidden, etc.
Is this to say that Rabbi Meir holds:
a person does not put himself
phrases.notes: The sentence finishes on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: it leaves the יובל discussion and turns to the next case in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי מאיר's ruling about a vow 'until פסח' show that he holds a person does not include a certain time in his vow?
